title: Diagram rules
examples: How do I label my diagram correctly?
What does it mean when the curve shifts?
Can you show me an example of equilibrium?

explain.say: Today we learn to draw economic diagrams properly. We need to label the axes first. The vertical axis usually shows price. The horizontal axis shows the quantity.
Next we find the equilibrium point on the diagram. This is where the supply and demand curves cross. At this point, the market is stable.
When demand increases, the entire demand curve shifts. We show this with an arrow to the right. This means people want more at every price.
If there is a decrease in supply, the supply curve shifts. We show this with an arrow to the left. This means producers make less at every price.
For a real-life example, think about strawberries. If they become very popular, demand increases. The demand curve shifts right, leading to a higher price and more quantity.
A common mistake is forgetting to label the new equilibrium. You must show the new crossing point. Always label the new price and quantity.

faq.q: Do I always use price on the vertical axis?
faq.a: Yes, for standard supply and demand diagrams, price is usually on the vertical axis. You could also use it for other types of graphs.
asks: Is the vertical axis always price?

faq.q: What does it mean when the curve shifts?
faq.a: A shift means that the relationship between price and quantity has changed, not just that the quantity changed at one price. It is a change in the underlying factors.
asks: Is a shift the same as moving along the curve?
What causes a curve to shift?
Does shifting mean the law changed?

faq.q: How do I show the shift direction?
faq.a: You use arrows to show the direction of the shift. A shift right means an increase, and a shift left means a decrease.
asks: What do arrows mean on the diagram?
Should I draw a new curve or use an arrow?
Does the arrow point to the change?

faq.q: Is the new equilibrium always higher?
faq.a: Not always. If demand increases but supply also increases, the new equilibrium price might stay the same. You must check both shifts.
asks: Can price go down after a shift?
Does the direction depend on the factors?

faq.q: What if I am drawing a different diagram, like costs?
faq.a: You must check the specific rules for that diagram. For cost diagrams, the axes might be different, but the principle of labeling remains the same.
asks: Does this apply to all economic diagrams?
Are the rules the same everywhere?

facts: The vertical axis typically represents Price (P).
The horizontal axis typically represents Quantity (Q).
An increase in demand causes the demand curve to shift to the right.
A decrease in supply causes the supply curve to shift to the left.

quiz.say: If the price of coffee rises, and the demand curve shifts right, what is the most likely outcome?
quiz.show: New Equilibrium: Higher Price, Higher Quantity
quiz.why: A rightward shift in demand increases both the equilibrium price and the equilibrium quantity.

wrong.0: This would happen if both supply and demand decreased together.
wrong.1: This pattern usually results from a decrease in supply, not an increase in demand.
wrong.2: This combination suggests a shift in supply that outpaces the demand increase.

quiz.say: When drawing a diagram, what must the horizontal axis always represent?
quiz.why: The horizontal axis is conventionally used to measure the amount or quantity of goods or services.

wrong.0: Time is usually shown on the horizontal axis only in time-series graphs.
wrong.1: Income is a factor that shifts the curve, not the axis label itself.
wrong.3: Price is the standard measurement for the vertical axis.

quiz.say: If the supply curve shifts left, what happens to the original equilibrium point?
quiz.show: Original E: Too high, Too low

options.show: The original equilibrium point is no longer valid.
options.say: The original equilibrium point is no longer valid.

options.show: It moves up and to the right.
options.say: It moves up and to the right.

options.show: It stays exactly where it was.
options.say: It stays exactly where it was.

options.show: It moves down and to the left.
options.say: It moves down and to the left.

quiz.why: A shift means the old point is incorrect because the market conditions have fundamentally changed.

wrong.1: This describes an increase in both supply and demand.
wrong.2: A shift means the relationship changes, so the point must move.
wrong.3: This would suggest a decrease in both supply and demand.
